findings.title: Handle imminent reminders before deferring cancellation to cron
findings.body: The default cancellation path only sets cancelled=true, leaving the email queued at SendGrid until the 15-minute cron runs. If a booking is cancelled at 10:01, its reminder is due at 10:10, and the next cron runs at 10:15, the reminder is still sent. The cron then deletes the overdue database row before attempting cancellation. Reminders close to their send time need synchronous cancellation rather than unconditional deferral.

findings.title: Rescheduling bypasses the new cancellation queue
findings.body: Every rescheduled booking passes immediateDelete=true for its old email reminders, bypassing the one-hour cancellation window. SendGrid retains these cancellation entries until their original send times, so rescheduling 100 reminders scheduled days ahead can still exhaust the pending-cancellation quota described in this PR. Subsequent requests fail, and the immediate branch only logs the error without setting cancelled=true, so cron never retries those reminders and they remain scheduled for the old booking.

findings.title: Persist successful cancellations and isolate failures per reminder
findings.body: The Prisma delete operations accumulated here are lazy and execute only in the Promise.all after every SendGrid request succeeds. If any cancellation request fails, the outer catch skips that Promise.all, leaving even successfully cancelled reminders in the database. It also skips every remaining reminder. A persistent error for one batch can therefore repeatedly block unrelated cancellations, allowing their emails to reach their send times. Delete each successfully cancelled row promptly and handle request failures per reminder.

findings.title: Await the database changes that record reminder cancellation
findings.body: Reminder deletion and cancellation-flag updates now happen inside the async reminder-manager functions, but these nested forEach calls discard their promises. The operations are also no longer included in the awaited prismaPromises, unlike the previous database deletions. Consequently, the handler can return success before unscheduled reminders are deleted or queued emails are marked cancelled. In a serverless invocation, outstanding writes can be suspended after the response, leaving reminders eligible to be scheduled or sent. Collect and await these cancellation promises.
